author: WP13
summary: Updated chapter on the glTF evidence system: specification pin, generated 148-asset corpus, the L0-L7 ladder, renderer-owned L7 campaigns, Khronos comparisons, the append-only defect ledger, loss reporting and milestone statuses. Largely current at TARGET; corrections add L0/Perf/Ledger/Tool CTest entries, the CI scope, the 13-asset reference subset, a ninth ledger record and the restated open ROBUST rows. The site had only one line of counts on the verification page; the full evidence model now lives on the glTF conformance deep dive.

sections.heading: The ladder, including its L0 gate

concepts.text: CNA's glTF support is an evidence system: pinned specification, deterministic committed corpus, numerical observations up to bound effect state, renderer-owned pixel campaigns and an append-only defect ledger.
tokens: an evidence system as much as an importer

concepts.text: The resulting claim is qualified: the import/runtime model is declared correct for the scoped campaign, not every optional extension, renderer shader or hostile input.
tokens: renderer coverage stated beside it rather than inside it

concepts.text: docs/gltf-conformance.md pins the Khronos glTF 2.0 specification at commit 2b29723d...222a, a 149,830-byte AsciiDoc with SHA-256 55986799...4b27967, pinned 2026-08-11, with a curl/sha256sum re-verification recipe.
The AsciiDoc source is pinned rather than a registry HTML snapshot because it is the generator input, has a stable digest and is retrievable at an immutable revision.
tokens: rather than a registry HTML snapshot

concepts.text: The specification is research and test authority, not vendored and not a build-time or run-time dependency.
The standard-library Python generator under tools/gltf_fixtures emits each fixture, its GLB twin, its expectations and any byte goldens from one source of truth.
tokens: one source of truth per fixture

concepts.text: Outputs are committed and guarded by manifest.json SHA-256 digests; CnaTests re-verifies digests so no Python is needed at test time; check-only regeneration must be byte-identical.
At TARGET tests/assets/gltf holds 148 .gltf assets, 148 .glb twins and 148 .expected.json records in a 744-file tree, in fifteen owning groups.

target.evidence: tests/assets/gltf/manifest.json (distinctAssetCount 148, owningGroupCounts); file count of tests/assets/gltf

concepts.text: The paired container audit examines 296 containers, while the validator gate classifies valid and expected-invalid cases separately; the denominators must not be merged into one number of glTF tests.
Each .expected.json keeps specification-derived L1-L4 expectations, a CNA-specific L5 section, and a defects list with first divergent layer, owning tasks and dated measured output.
CI proves every committed glTF asset is CNA-generated (provenance script), regenerates the corpus with --check and runs the generator twice for determinism.
The Khronos validator is pinned (validator-pin.json) and fetched for the corpus gate but is not needed to build or run CNA.
concepts.note: At TARGET the validator gate runs in CI.

concepts.text: Khronos Sample Assets and the Sample Renderer are fetched on demand for bounded comparisons, never redistributed or made runtime dependencies.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: The semantic ladder has seven layers; a separate L0 gate proves corpus and oracle machinery intact, and a higher layer is meaningful only when lower ones agree.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L1 observes container structure: parser counts, selected scene, relationships and declared extensions.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L2 observes decoded accessor arrays after offsets, strides, normalization and sparse overrides.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L3 observes semantic import: streams, materials, topology, grouping, skins, animation and reportable loss before packing.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L4 observes composed geometry after node and skin coordinate rules.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L5 observes GPU vertex and index bytes with field-aware diagnostics.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L6 observes bound effect state reaching GpuDrawParams through the same virtual FillGpuDrawParams call a draw makes, stopping before rasterization.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L7 observes rendered pixels per renderer with explicit safe-rejection dispositions.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: The ladder is registered as separate CTest entries CnaGltfConformanceL0 to L6 plus Perf, Ledger and Tool under the gltf-conformance label, lowest first, so the first failing entry names the first divergent layer.
concepts.note: The claim said L1-L6; TARGET registers L0 and three extra entries too.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: The rung list is a single source of truth: GltfConformanceLadder parses it and asserts every Gltf* suite belongs to exactly one rung.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L5 has 140 byte-golden fixtures; eight have none: seven deliberate rejections and one generated-tangent case whose generator refuses to duplicate the production algorithm as its oracle.

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: The L5 comparator's own tests prove it reports a perturbed byte at the right offset/field/vertex, truncation at the first missing byte and unknown strides without guessing.
tokens: truncation at the first missing byte

concepts.section: The ladder, including its L0 gate
concepts.text: L6 deliberately excludes the device's buffer additions and records alpha mode, cutoff and double-sidedness beside the block so carried and bound stay distinct; L6 is what exposed D7.
Four whole-corpus L7 reports are retained: OPENGLES3/EasyGL (Mesa llvmpipe), VULKAN, SOFTWARE and DIRECTX11 under Wine with DXVK 2.6.0, captured 2026-08-18 at CNA b6c180fd.
Each report gives all 148 assets a disposition: 140 deterministic captures and eight safe rejections.
Each renderer owns its goldens at tolerance 0 and requires two independent viewer processes to agree byte for byte; no renderer borrows another's image or tolerance.
These campaigns are recorded evidence present in the tree, not reproduced here; same-renderer repeatability is not an independent implementation oracle.

Automatically, the glTF renderer conformance workflow runs the ladder and stride conformance on STUB, HEADLESS, OPENGLES3, VULKAN and SOFTWARE and an L7 job on OPENGLES3 through an external pinned viewer; a sanitizer workflow runs STUB with ASan/UBSan, Draco on and off.
concepts.note: Adds TARGET's CI scope, which the claim did not state.

concepts.text: A 13-asset comparison with the pinned Khronos sample renderer (2026-08-15) gates IoU >= 0.99, coverage within [0.99,1.01] and RGB MAE <= 80; all passed, minimum IoU 0.999579.
concepts.note: The claim described only the retake matrix; the 13-asset subset is the independent check.

concepts.text: The reference comparison caught a real renderer defect: EasyGL's lit program evaluated specular maths for an unlit effect, normalize(0) produced NaNs and RGB error 189.33.
The final viewer retake (2026-08-14) runs 14 gate rows as 15 captures against pinned Khronos sample assets with explicit silhouette, coverage and colour-error thresholds; all passed.
The retake is broader than a smoke test and narrower than pixel-identical proof of all 148 fixtures.
Normative expectations and measured behaviour are separate fields; a known-defect test asserts the expectation is unmet and the divergence equals the recorded one.
tokens: CNA broken in the documented way

concepts.text: Records move known-failing -> partially-remediated -> fixed; a fix moves the old measurement to priorActual and records are never deleted; a bidirectional completeness test guards the bookkeeping.
D1-D3 (node TRS, hierarchy, matrix transforms) are fixed.
D4 (sparse index accessors decoded as zero) is fixed.
tokens: sparse index accessors decoded as zeros

concepts.text: D5 (topology) is fixed: point/line topology carried, loops/strips/fans converted explicitly.
tokens: D5 now carries point and line topology

concepts.text: D6 (rigid node animation dropped) is fixed for unskinned models; the remaining mixed-carrier loss is reported.
D7 (factor-only PBR material lost) is fixed and reaches the L6 material contract and recorded campaigns.
tokens: D7 reaches the L6 material contract

concepts.text: D8 (ancestry above a skin's joint set lost) is fixed by the separate root prefix.
The ledger at TARGET has a ninth record, GLTF-241 (vertex-coloured metallic-roughness primitive), also fixed.

GltfImportReportEXT is part of the public CNAEXT surface on direct and converter-produced CNJ models: counts plus ordered diagnostic codes; AnythingLost and dropped/approximated counts distinguish a successful load from a lossless one; branch on codes, not messages.
The runtime model exposes skin mappings, cameras, variant names and selection, whole-model bounds and per-part topology, closing old parsed-but-unreachable gaps.
Deliberate limits remain: two UV sets per PBR primitive; four influences and a 72-matrix palette; point/spot lights approximated with range and cone lost.
tokens: at most two distinct texture-coordinate sets per PBR primitive

concepts.text: EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing imports one placement per node and EXT_meshopt_compression is refused without a decoder.
KTX2/BasisU and WebP need a PNG/JPEG fallback; mirrored placements are reported but left to the application's cull state.
tokens: KTX2/BasisU and WebP images need a PNG/JPEG fallback

concepts.text: The plan records GLTF CORE 2.0 IMPORT/RUNTIME MODEL CORRECT (2026-08-18), covering importer, CNJ route, model graph, effect/state transport, corpus and recorded renderer evidence; an earlier unqualified name was withdrawn.

GLTF ROBUST is recorded as 9 of 12 rows with three open: KHR_materials_specular texture sampling (at TARGET only METAL among current renderers lacks it), native point/spot lights, and a fourth renderer on the retake matrix (three qualify, including DIRECTX11 under Wine/DXVK).
concepts.note: Row 1 restated for the current renderer set; renderers outside the 25 identities are not named.

concepts.text: Native point/spot lighting is the only open row that is a whole feature, because it needs a shared light ABI that XNA's IEffectLights cannot express.
tokens: the only open row that is a whole feature

concepts.text: The open rows do not contradict the qualified core declaration; they explain why the stronger milestone stays open.
tokens: do not contradict the qualified core declaration

concepts.text: Reading rule: a green import plus an empty loss report establishes the represented model, L5 the bytes, L6 what reaches an effect, and only renderer-engaged pixel evidence the final image on that renderer and host.
tokens: only renderer-engaged pixel evidence establishes the final image

issues.text: Native point and spot lights with range and cone are not implemented; glTF punctual lights are approximated as up to three directional lights (GLTF ROBUST row 6).
METAL does not sample the KHR_materials_specular texture maps (factor-only).
Whole-corpus L7 campaigns for VULKAN, SOFTWARE and DIRECTX11 are recorded reports (2026-08-18, CNA b6c180fd), not CI-run; only the OPENGLES3 L7 rung runs in CI, through an external pinned viewer.
The bounded Khronos retake matrix qualifies three renderers (OPENGLES3, VULKAN, DIRECTX11 under Wine/DXVK); a fourth is pending (GLTF ROBUST row 12).
